user_goal: Turn PLOTKEEPER into a first-class Git repository with examples, screenshots, usage and installation documentation, and easy implementation instructions.

authority.verbatim_text: Okay, so PLOTKEEPER - can we turn that into a first-class git repo with examples, screenshots, usage/installation docs and easy to implement instructions??

baseline.protection_evidence: Clean local main checkout with a single worktree; git status reported no changed files before task mutation.
baseline.selection_reason: Current clean main HEAD predates all repository-productization changes in this task.

semantic_changes: Make installation and startup portable outside the Z drive source checkout.
Add repository-facing documentation, examples, screenshots, and validation needed to prove the documented workflow.
Add packaging metadata and tests directly required for the documented install and usage paths.

paths: Windows registry locations other than an explicit local installation smoke test
semantic_changes: Do not weaken Plotkeeper's read-only session observation or review-closeout gates.
Do not publish, push, merge, deploy, or create a remote repository without separate user authority.
Do not add a guessed software license or claim unsupported platform compatibility.

invariants: Plotkeeper never writes to Codex session JSONL inputs.
A run closes only after the existing injected terminal PASS receipt requirements are met.
Existing runtime data remains preserved and uncommitted.
Documented commands must match executable repository behavior.

acceptance_cases.promised_behavior: A Windows user can install and start Plotkeeper from a fresh repository checkout using the documented commands.
acceptance_cases.forbidden_behavior: Installation must not depend on the original Z drive path or modify Codex session files.
acceptance_cases.target_and_actor: Windows user operating a fresh local clone with Python 3.11 or newer.

acceptance_cases.promised_behavior: A new adopter can understand what Plotkeeper does, run a self-contained example, and integrate it with SpecSwarm from repository documentation.
acceptance_cases.forbidden_behavior: Documentation must not present unverified commands, hidden machine-specific prerequisites, or invented behavior.
acceptance_cases.target_and_actor: Developer reading the repository without prior Plotkeeper context.

acceptance_cases.promised_behavior: The repository includes current desktop and mobile screenshots that visibly demonstrate the dashboard.
acceptance_cases.forbidden_behavior: Screenshots must not be mockups presented as live application evidence.
acceptance_cases.target_and_actor: Repository visitor evaluating Plotkeeper before installation.

proof_requirements.claim: The Python project installs into an isolated environment and exposes its documented command.
proof_requirements.required_environment: Fresh isolated Python environment on Windows
proof_requirements.command_or_read_only_check: Install from the repository and run the documented CLI help and health path.
proof_requirements.expected_observation: Installation succeeds without importing from the source checkout and the CLI starts successfully.

proof_requirements.claim: Existing backend, dashboard, and read-only gate behavior remains green.
proof_requirements.command_or_read_only_check: Run the complete automated test suite plus static compilation checks.
proof_requirements.expected_observation: All tests and compilation checks pass with no tracked runtime database.

proof_requirements.claim: The quickstart, usage, architecture, configuration, troubleshooting, and integration instructions are internally linked and command-accurate.
proof_requirements.command_or_read_only_check: Audit every documented local path and command against repository files and smoke-test the quickstart.
proof_requirements.expected_observation: Links resolve and commands produce the documented result.

proof_requirements.claim: At least one self-contained example exercises a real Plotkeeper workflow without private session data.
proof_requirements.required_environment: Temporary directory on the Z drive
proof_requirements.command_or_read_only_check: Execute the example and inspect its generated API or CLI result.
proof_requirements.expected_observation: The example completes deterministically and exposes a populated demonstration run.

proof_requirements.claim: Desktop and mobile screenshots are captured from a running Plotkeeper instance populated by the repository example.
proof_requirements.required_environment: Local browser against the running example service
proof_requirements.command_or_read_only_check: Capture and inspect desktop and mobile viewport screenshots.
proof_requirements.expected_observation: Both images render the live dashboard legibly and correspond to the documented example.

release_requirements.required_receipt: No publication or deployment is authorized; a separate user-authorized release contract is required.

stop_conditions: The checkout becomes dirty from an unrelated actor or an unexpected path enters the diff.
A required documented workflow cannot be proven without changing a forbidden semantic surface.
The existing read-only or review-closeout invariants regress.
Publication, remote creation, push, merge, deployment, or licensing becomes necessary without explicit user authority.
known_discrepancies: The repository has no configured Git remote.
The current README uses a machine-specific Z drive installation command.
The checkpoint references an older tested head than the current clean main HEAD.
No repository license is present; no license will be inferred.

requirement_trace.user_requirement: usage and installation docs with easy implementation instructions
